title: Rebaseline console insight surface: compact dashboards + sampled tracing for MVP
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Purpose: narrow the Console observability surface so we can ship an actionable MVP within the next sprint without compromising core SLAs. This ticket captures specific scope cuts, acceptance criteria, reasoning, and the rollout plan for Dashboard cards, tracing sampling, and route-level cost views.

Context: multiple high-cost dashboard tiles and full-span tracing were stretching implementation and infra budgets. Product, Eng, and Design agreed to a surgical reduction: prioritize a compact set of route-centric cost cards, a single lightweight tracing panel with sampled spans and guided drilldowns, and defer advanced joiners/aggregation and long-retention telemetry to post-MVP.

Goals:
- Deliver a usable Console MVP that surfaces per-route cost spikes and simple latency distributions.
- Keep implementation bounded: avoid heavy aggregation work and long tail trace storage in the MVP.
- Provide a clear migration path for later phases (A/B rollouts for expanded tiles and retention).
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: three compact cards implemented for a route: total token spend (24h), median latency (24h), and error rate (24h), with per-route filter and link-to-inspector

Cost calculation: per-route token spend calculated using cached route->model mapping; cost unit uses the current pricing table and matches finance sample queries (within 5% of billing dashboard for test dataset)
Tracing: default sampling at 10% globally, with on-demand sample escalation for a selected route (one-click); UI shows sampled span count and indicates sampling rate
Performance: UI queries for the compact dashboard return within 350ms p95 for 90% of synthetic test routes under staging traffic profile
Storage: tracing retention for MVP spans limited to 48 hours and flagged in docs; longer retention paths are gated behind a future storage/infra ticket
Rollout: feature flag exists (console.obs.compact_mvp) and can be toggled per-org; canary tested with 5% of traffic and rollback plan documented
Docs: PRD and public quickstart updated with screenshots and an explicit Upgrade/Pivot section describing what is deferred
QA: automated smoke tests for the three cards and sampled tracing flow are added to the console test harness and pass on staging
notes: 2026-02-26 — Kickoff: alignment meeting with Eng (Samir Rao), Design (Marina Lopez) and Observability PMs. Agreed to prioritize route-level cost because downstream billing and customer tickets indicated high signal.
2026-03-02 — Trade-off: deferred joiner work (route -> user attribution across services) to keep query complexity low; accepted that some multi-service cost attributions will be missing in MVP.
2026-03-04 — Design review: provided compact card mocks (drive: https://drive.redwood/console/compact-mvp-mocks) and microcopy for sampling indicator. Design signed off for dev scope reduction.

2026-03-06 — Eng feasibility: ENG owners flagged two infra blockers (ENG-24187: cheap KV cache for per-route mapping; ENG-24300: sampled-span ingestion endpoint). Added as dependencies and requested 2-sprint delivery target.
2026-03-09 — Security: confirmed no additional telemetry encryption changes required for 48h tracing retention; will require infra review if retention is increased.
2026-03-10 — PM decision: acceptance criteria finalized, changed sampling default to 10% (was 5%) to improve debug signal while keeping cost controlled.
implementation_notes: Implement dashboard as three lightweight endpoints that reuse existing route index table; avoid full materialized aggregation in first pass.
Tracing: add a sampling flag to the span ingestion lambda; sampled spans routed to short-term S3 bucket + index for 48h retrieval
Feature flag: console.obs.compact_mvp must gate both UI and backend behaviors; ensure canary and org-level toggles
Observability: add cost telemetry for per-request sampling multiplier to track debug cost impact
testing_plan: Unit tests for per-route cost computation including fallback when a route->model mapping is stale
Staging e2e with 10k synthetic requests across 20 routes to verify p95 query latencies and sampling behavior
Manual UX validation with design checklist for microcopy and sampling indicator behavior
rollback_plan: Toggle feature flag off to remove UI; revert ingestion sampling change via deployment rollback playbook; alert on increased error rates
Postmortem template ready in case of cost/regression incidents
